To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) LASSO local model averaging (LLARMA) provides an effective method for characterizing the uncertainty in model choice in the presence of strong LD; 2) LLARMA is applicable to any model selection procedure that can be used to fit a model with a single SNP; and 3) LLARMA provides a useful tool for prioritizing SNPs in a region of association.

(1) when there are several underlying true signals and strong LD, LASSO-based resample model averaging is more effective than single-locus analysis and the recently proposed Stability Selection for identifying the set of SNPs that includes true signals, (2) the performance of the proposed method is not affected by the number of SNPs, and (3) the performance of LASSO-based methods can be further enhanced by using multiple imputation for the missing data in the LASSO-based models

the LLARRMA method is a powerful and robust approach to reprioritization of SNPs in hit regions, which is applicable to GWAS data and can provide a useful complement to single SNP analysis.
LASSO local auto-regularization resample model averaging is a useful tool in the context of GWAS.
the LLARRMA is a powerful and flexible method that allows for the identification of multiple causal variants and the estimation of their effects, even under conditions of strong LD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LLARRMA is a method for characterizing the uncertainty in model selection in the presence of strong linkage disequilibrium.
LLARRMA is a method for reprioritizing genetic associations in regions where there is strong LD and there is a high likelihood that multiple loci are involved.
we have developed a method to identify a set of SNPs within a region that are likely to contain the causal variant.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to use a simple, easily implemented, and flexible resampling-based model-averaging approach to reprioritize the set of genetic variants within a hit region that are most likely to be causal.

, in the presence of strong linkage disequilibrium, single‐loci methods are not reliable for prioritizing SNPs within regions that have been identified as “hits” by initial genome‐wide association scans.

, in the presence of strong LD and multiple causal loci, the LASSO can be a useful first step in identifying a set of candidate SNPs, but it can be improved by a post-LASSO step that characterizes model uncertainty in a principled way.
